title: FairMatch: Promoting Partial Label Learning by Unlabeled Samples

problem.claim: The paper studies semi-supervised partial label learning, which seeks to improve partial label learning by leveraging unlabeled samples.

gap.claim: Confidence-based selection of unlabeled samples can become unfair across classes because labeled samples are scarce and partial labels are ambiguous, especially early in training, causing slower training and performance degradation.

contributions.claim: FairMatch uses a learning-state-aware self-adaptive threshold to select the same number of high-confidence unlabeled samples from each class and applies augmentation consistency to incorporate them.
FairMatch uses candidate label disambiguation for partially labeled samples and mixes them with selected high-confidence unlabeled samples to reduce overfitting on partial-label samples.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe FairMatch as a novel method.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report maximum accuracy improvements of 9.53% on CIFAR-10, 4.9% on CIFAR-100, and 16.45% on CIFAR-100H.
The authors report that code is available in a GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: The work addresses semi-supervised partial label learning using unlabeled samples.
Existing methods select high-confidence unlabeled samples as pseudo labels using the maximum model output.
Label scarcity and partial-label ambiguity can bias selection across classes, slowing training and reducing performance.
FairMatch combines class-balanced adaptive thresholding, augmentation consistency, candidate label disambiguation, and mixing of partial and selected unlabeled samples.
The authors report maximum accuracy improvements on three CIFAR datasets and provide a code repository.

source_observation.claim: Confidence-based pseudo-label selection can be skewed toward some classes when labels are scarce and partial labels are ambiguous.

interpretation.claim: Selection policies may need to account for class balance and training state rather than relying only on a global confidence ranking.

application.claim: For semi-supervised classification, consider adaptive class-balanced thresholds together with consistency-based use of unlabeled data.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond the reported partial-label learning setting or datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluation baselines, experimental protocols, or statistical variation.
The abstract does not provide details of the threshold schedule, augmentation design, or label-disambiguation procedure.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility of the reported improvements.
